conflicts.point: Whether a catastrophic LLM-exfiltration tail with no claims history can be actuarially priced at all, which determines whether the mutualized insurance pool can form and self-fund the standing audit it requires.

positions.stance: Cyber-insurers (Lloyd's syndicates) already price correlated breach tails via scenario modeling without complete loss history; the output-extraction red-team supplies a measurable extraction rate that becomes the simulation input, so continuous attestation re-underwrites the policy as the surface changes.

Agrees the tail is priceable by scenario simulation, citing the 2019 Lloyd's/Cambridge 'Bashe' $193B modeled scenario; the red-team's measured extraction curve times population times statutory penalty yields a reservable ex-ante loss event.

LLM memorization has no defined event boundary and no record count until probed, so there is no loss-development triangle to reserve against; scenario models for credential dumps have bounded record counts while the memorization surface is unbounded until an attacker writes the prompt, making any reserve a guess in a suit.

conflicts.point: Whether the entity that runs/funds the continuous red-team can be made independent enough to disclose its own leaks, given that the discoverer's premium rises when it reports.

positions.stance: Separate who pays from who appoints, as Sarbanes-Oxley/PCAOB did (issuer-paid but board-controlled audits), and convert discovery into a legal duty under an SEC/NHTSA-style mandatory incident registry so concealment, not disclosure, carries the penalty.

An insurer must independently re-derive red-team findings rather than accept self-reported results, which requires a standing technical corps with live model access at every frontier provider across continuous retraining; if the industry funds it the watchdog conflict re-emerges one level up, and if a public corps does it, no appropriation has been named or costed.

conflicts.point: Whether output-extraction red-teaming can price the prevention failure, i.e., whether a firm that cross-references and memorizes produces a measurably leakier extraction surface that the premium can capture.

positions.stance: A cross-referencing, memorizing firm has a demonstrably leakier extraction surface, so the market prices the prevention failure through the detection surface and voluntary siloing emerges as a priced incentive without a Congressional input mandate.

Signing the input stream proves what entered training but not what the model memorized and can regurgitate; the completeness problem relocates to the output boundary where it is harder, because the memorization surface is whatever a sufficiently clever prompt pulls loose, discovered only by probing after deployment against a model retrained every few weeks.

verdicts.conflict: Whether a catastrophic LLM-exfiltration tail with no claims history can be actuarially priced well enough to fund a self-sustaining audit pool.
verdicts.rationale: The accelerationist and safetyist conflate scenario-modeling a bounded event (a credential dump with N known records) with reserving against an open-ended memorization surface that has no record count until an attacker probes it. The skeptic identifies the decisive disanalogy: the Bashe scenario and Lloyd's cyber tails rest on countable exposed entities, while LLM regurgitation has no defined loss boundary, so any reserve is an unfalsifiable guess. The accelerationist's 'measurable extraction rate' assumes the very completeness the skeptic shows is missing—you only know what you measured, not what an unrun prompt would pull loose.

verdicts.conflict: Whether the entity that runs and funds continuous red-teaming can be made independent enough to disclose its own discovered leaks.
verdicts.rationale: The safetyist points to a working precedent—PCAOB and Sarbanes-Oxley separate who pays (the issuer) from who appoints and controls (an independent board), and SEC/NHTSA mandatory incident registries make concealment, not disclosure, the punishable act. That structurally answers the conflict-of-interest problem with an existing institutional template rather than asserting it is unsolvable. The skeptic raises a real cost-and-access objection—standing technical corps with live frontier-model access across continuous retraining—but offers no reason the PCAOB design fails, only that it is expensive and unappropriated, which is a fundability point, not an independence-impossibility point.

verdicts.conflict: Whether output-extraction red-teaming can price the prevention failure so that voluntary siloing emerges without a Congressional input mandate.
verdicts.rationale: The accelerationist's claim that a cross-referencing, memorizing firm has a 'demonstrably leakier' surface that the market will price requires that probing reliably reveals the leak before deployment, but the skeptic shows the completeness problem just relocates to the output boundary where it is harder. Signing the input stream proves what entered training, not what the model memorized and can regurgitate, and the memorization surface is whatever a clever prompt extracts—discovered only by probing a model retrained every few weeks. The accelerationist needs the detection surface to be roughly complete for the market signal to track real risk, and that premise is exactly what fails.
